subtitle: mass in a good enough Riemannian manifold is non-negative
summary: The Positive Mass Theorem in general relativity
problem: As a cornerstone of mathematical general relativity, the Positive Mass Theorem asserts that for any complete, smooth, connected 3-dimensional asymptotically flat Riemannian manifold with non-negative scalar curvature, the total gravitational (ADM) mass is non-negative, and vanishes if and only if the manifold is isometric to flat Euclidean space ℝ³. Landmark proofs of this theorem via minimal surfaces (by Schoen and Yau) and spinors (by Witten) were central to the Fields Medals awarded to both Shing-Tung Yau (1982) and Edward Witten (1990). Using LEAP, we formalize this celebrated theorem end-to-end by following the modern harmonic-function level-set approach of Bray, Kazaras, Khuri, and Stern (https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.06754).
statement: Let `(M, g)` be a smooth connected complete asymptotically flat Riemannian 3-manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature. Then for every end the ADM mass `m` exists and satisfies `m ≥ 0`, and `m = 0` if and only if `(M, g)` is isometric to `(ℝ³, δ)`.
title: Harmonic Functions and the Mass of 3-Dimensional Asymptotically Flat Riemannian Manifolds
